title: What the action principle buys
promptMarkdown: In your own words, and without the notes open, explain in under 200 words what Hamilton's principle gives you that $\mathbf F = m\ddot{\mathbf r}$ does not, for (a) a change of coordinates and (b) a system with a holonomic constraint. Then name one kind of force that the recipe $L = T - V$ does not handle directly and say in one sentence how such forces are accommodated.
hintLadder: What happened to the centripetal term when you wrote the polar-coordinate Lagrangian, compared with writing Newton's law in polar coordinates?
In the cone example, which force was never computed? Why was that allowed?
Think of a block sliding on a rough table. Is there a potential whose gradient gives the friction force?

criteria.criterion: Explains that the Euler–Lagrange equations keep their form in any coordinates, so acceleration terms such as the centripetal term appear automatically.
Explains that holonomic, frictionless constraints are absorbed by choosing independent coordinates, so constraint forces need not be computed.
Names a non-potential force (friction, air drag, or a general velocity-dependent force) and says it is added as a generalized force on the right-hand side (or via D'Alembert's principle).

levels.label: not met
levels.description: Missing or wrong (e.g. claims every force has a potential).
